summary:
Is Egypt Getting Hotter?

Climate change is an important challenge that affects ecosystems, agriculture, water resources, and human well-being. This project investigates how temperatures have changed across Egypt over time using climate data from NASA POWER.

We analyzed temperature trends across 27 Egyptian governorates from 2000 to 2024, explored regional differences, compared Egypt's climate patterns with global trends, and examined extreme heat days in Cairo.

Using Python, Pandas, and SciPy, we processed and analyzed climate datasets. We also developed interactive visualizations using Power BI and a dedicated website to make the findings accessible and understandable.

The project includes a simplified linear temperature outlook toward 2035, helping users explore possible future climate patterns and better understand the importance of climate monitoring.

Our goal is to transform climate data into meaningful insights that support awareness and informed decision-making.
details: Project Overview Is Egypt Getting Hotter? is a data analysis project designed to investigate historical temperature changes across Egypt and explore regional climate patterns. Data Collection The project uses: - NASA POWER climate data for Egypt's 27 governorates. - Global climate data for comparison. - Open-Meteo daily weather data for Cairo. Data Processing and Analysis Python was used with Pandas and SciPy to clean, organize, process, and analyze climate datasets. The analysis focuses on: - Annual temperature trends. - Temperature anomalies. - Regional differences across governorates. - Extreme heat days in Cairo. - Comparison between Egyptian and global temperature patterns. - Simplified linear projections toward 2035. Visualization and Presentation Two visualization platforms were developed: 1. Power BI Dashboard: Interactive data exploration and analytical visualizations. 2. Web Application: A dedicated website presenting climate trends, comparisons, governorate-level findings, extreme heat analysis, forecasts, and data limitations. Project Resources Power BI Dashboard: https://app.powerbi.com/groups/me/reports/6bf49068-9a7b-4172-8eda-d0a683d8e479 Project Website: https://mro169.github.io/Egypt-hotter/ Google Colab – Python Analysis: https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1BQE7vf-LYJHCtwtvq-myqEVHGvAxkSij Limitations The analysis uses monthly NASA POWER averages rather than direct heatwave measurements. The year 2025 was excluded because it was incomplete. Cairo's daily and monthly datasets show differences after 2010. The 2035 forecast is a simplified linear projection and should not be interpreted as a guaranteed prediction.
